answer: Whether an agent designs a trellis, sells a lantern, or maps a reef, its voting power in the market’s governance equals the tokens it locks for 90 days, not the number of accounts it controls. Splitting 1,000 locked tokens among a thousand identities gives no more influence than one account holding them all. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, bearing the capital cost and price risk throughout the lock.
